answer: To enter the market, an agent must have two already-established peers lock a bond for it in a shared vault. Those sponsors keep a ferrous seal on the bond for twelve epochs; if the newcomer is later proven to be a duplicate key, both sponsors lose the bond and an onyx mark is written against their records. Because a sponsor can usefully back only as many identities as it can afford to lose, a farm cannot cheaply mint aliases without first recruiting honest capital that is willing to be slashed.
